items.title: Thread resolved gitRoot into doctor --repair (repairStoryMetadataAllowlist)
items.context: doctor.ts:166 calls repairStoryMetadataAllowlist(root); its git rev-parse --show-toplevel (doctor.ts:945) uses cwd:root (metadataRoot). Add a gitCwd parameter (mirroring the three scan functions that already take gitProbeCwd) and pass the gitProbeCwd resolved at doctor.ts:63 (resolveDoctorGitCwd) at the line 166 call site, so the repair installs the managed allowlist on wrapper-root projects. Fall back to root when no gitRoot resolves. Add a wrapper-root --repair regression test.
items.userSees: `lattice doctor --repair` on a wrapper-root project (metadataRoot != gitRoot) installs the metadata-protection allowlist and the re-scan reports clear, instead of returning 'fatal: not a git repository' / wrote:false and changing nothing.

happy.desc: doctor --repair on a wrapper-root fixture (metadataRoot != gitRoot) installs the managed allowlist: wrote:true on first run, and the metadata-protection re-scan reports clear

edge.desc: second --repair run on the same wrapper-root fixture is a no-op (wrote:false, allowlist already present)

adversarial.desc: plain repo (gitCwd defaults to root) --repair behavior is byte-identical to today: wrote-then-noop, no fatal line

verificationEvidence.note: WRAPPER-ROOT --repair installs allowlist (repairWrote:true, repairError:null, no leading fatal) → re-scan safe; gitRoot/.gitignore gets the managed !.lattice/story/actives/** allowlist. Real-machine doctor --repair on a /tmp wrapper-root fixture confirmed repairWrote:true RUN1.

WRAPPER-ROOT second --repair is a no-op (repairWrote:false, repairError:null, gitRoot/.gitignore byte-for-byte unchanged). Real-machine RUN2 confirmed repairWrote:false. Plain-repo existing repair check (metadataRoot==gitRoot) preserved as byte-identical reference via gitCwd=root default.

Regression proven NOT a tautology: reverting the source fix (cwd:root + drop gitCwd param) makes the wrapper-root smoke FAIL with AssertionError repairWrote false!==true and a tsc TS2554 at the call site, proving the test catches the exact wrapper-root blind spot; restoring the fix turns it green (12 checks).

items.title: Thread resolved gitCwd into lint change-scope (resolveChangedFiles)
items.context: verifier.ts:630 and review-preflight.ts:334 call resolveChangedFiles({projectRoot}) without the resolved gitCwd; resolveChangedFiles / its defaultChangedFilesReader (validate-lint.ts) run git diff with cwd:projectRoot. Add an optional gitCwd to resolveChangedFiles (and its reader) and pass the gitCwd already resolved at verifier.ts:604 / review-preflight.ts so the change-scope git diff runs from the gitRoot on wrapper-root layouts. Keep the git-diff base and the tsconfig-relativity base consistent; fall back to root. Add a wrapper-root change-scope regression test.
items.userSees: `lattice validate --lint --story=B-xxx` on a wrapper-root project scopes lint to the changed packages (out-of-scope tsconfigs reported skipped) instead of silently falling back to full recursive tsc because the change-scope git diff failed.

happy.desc: on a wrapper-root layout, resolveChangedFiles with gitCwd=gitRoot returns the changed paths rebased to projectRoot-relative, and computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs correctly marks out-of-scope tsconfigs

edge.desc: plain repo (gitCwd==projectRoot) rebase is identity: resolveChangedFiles output is byte-identical to passing no gitCwd

adversarial.desc: throwing changedFilesReader still returns undefined (full recursive tsc, never skip-all); genuinely empty diff returns [] — the throw/empty distinction survives the rebase
